Forest plot style (plot_forest)

Source: R/style_presets.R
style_forest.Rd

Default ggstylekit::style_spec() for plot_forest() / plot_build_forest(). Series names are the plot roles: point (the estimate), errorbar (the CI line range), ref_point (the estimate of a reference row: a reference copy in a covariate panel or the reference panel; an open circle by default), ref_line (the vertical reference line drawn at ref), and ref_band (the equivalence band drawn at ref_band; a geom_rect annotation whose fill and alpha come from the fill / alphas maps).

Usage

style_forest(...)

Arguments

...

Fields passed to ggstylekit::style_spec(), overriding the preset defaults; call the preset with no arguments to view them. Per-series maps merge entry-wise onto the defaults (e.g. shapes = c(point = 18) leaves the other roles unchanged; colors = c(FOOD = "red") adds a covariate color while keeping the role colors); all other fields replace their default wholesale. A palette function(n) in colors colours every covariate (called with the number of covariates); it replaces the role entries, which then fall back to the ggplot2 defaults.

Value

A ggstylekit_style_spec object.

Details

Per-covariate coloring is opt-in through the same colors map: add entries keyed by covariate name (the values of the cov_name_var column, e.g. colors = c(FOOD = "darkgreen", WTBL = "darkblue")). When at least one covariate present in the plotted data has an entry, the builder maps point and error bar color to the covariate (facet) and suppresses the legend, since the facet strips already label each covariate. Covariates without an entry take colours from the house palette, as for col_var in plot_dvtime(). The point, errorbar, and ref_point role colours are then replaced by the covariate colour; the reference panel keeps the ref_point colour unless colors names it. ref_line is unaffected.

The builder draws the covariate row facet itself (facet_grid(rows = cov_name, switch = "y")), so the facet* fields are ignored. It labels the x-axis with the rendered metric unless the xlabel field is supplied, and draws no title unless the title field is supplied. The house theme uses the forest panel variant of theme_bw(): a faint vertical ruler, no horizontal gridlines, covariate panels stacked without spacing into one frame, bold top-left covariate strips placed outside the y-axis, and the estimate column as right-hand axis text under a bold header drawn as the right-aligned subtitle on the top edge of the panels (style them through theme = with axis.text.y.right and plot.subtitle). Set logx = TRUE for a log x-axis.

Intervals are drawn as uncapped lines. Set the errorbar_width field to draw capped error bars instead; it is the cap height in row heights (e.g. style_forest(errorbar_width = 0.3), where 1 spans a full row). The preset leaves it unset, which the builder back-fills to 0 (no cap).

See also

style_forest_pmforest(), style_forest_coveffectsplot(), style_forest_pmxforest(), and style_forest_pumas() for the looks of the pmforest, coveffectsplot, and PMXForest packages and of Pumas.

Other forest plot: df_forest(), df_forest_preprocess(), is_forest_stats(), plot_build_forest(), plot_forest(), style_forest_coveffectsplot(), style_forest_pmforest(), style_forest_pmxforest(), style_forest_pumas()
